security_audit.summary: All 20 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences or benign metric text, with no executable Ruby or shell commands present. The skill does introduce moderate privacy and disclosure risks by requesting historical interaction analysis and visible reasoning traces without handling safeguards.

remediation.issue: Historical user interaction analysis lacks privacy and access-control guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Require authorized, minimized, and redacted datasets with defined retention limits before collecting or evaluating user interactions.

remediation.issue: The workflow requests visible reasoning traces for debugging.
remediation.suggestion: Use concise decision summaries and structured diagnostics that exclude hidden reasoning, system prompts, secrets, and private context.

content.value_statement: Agent changes often lack reliable evidence, testing, and rollout controls. This skill provides a measured workflow for analysis, prompt refinement, evaluation, deployment, and monitoring.
actual_capabilities: Defines baseline metrics for task success, accuracy, latency, token use, and user satisfaction.
Classifies failures by instruction, context, format, tool, constraint, and edge-case causes.
Guides targeted prompt revisions using examples, role definitions, self-checks, and output formats.
Designs representative test suites and controlled A/B comparisons with acceptance metrics.
Plans versioned rollouts with monitoring, rollback triggers, and post-deployment reviews.
Establishes weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual improvement cycles.
limitations: Requires representative metrics, feedback, or test cases from an existing agent.
Does not implement evaluation tools, dashboards, deployment systems, or data pipelines.
Suggested thresholds need adjustment for each environment, risk profile, and traffic level.
Human review remains necessary for subjective quality, safety, and production decisions.

use_cases.title: Improve Support Agent Reliability
use_cases.description: Analyze recurring corrections, refine response rules, and test revisions before a controlled customer rollout.

use_cases.title: Reduce Agent Cost and Latency
use_cases.description: Compare prompt variants against token use, response time, task success, and quality thresholds.

use_cases.title: Build an Agent Evaluation Program
use_cases.description: Create test categories, review rubrics, version records, rollout gates, and recurring performance reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Agent Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this agent using the supplied metrics and examples. Identify the three highest-impact failure modes and define measurable baseline indicators.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with existing results and representative failures.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Prompt Improvements
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the agent prompt, failure examples, and constraints. Propose targeted revisions, expected effects, and regression tests for each change.
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn diagnosed failures into focused prompt changes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Controlled Evaluation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an A/B evaluation for the original and revised agents using [test set]. Define metrics, sample allocation, acceptance thresholds, and review steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare prompt versions before production deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Production Optimization Cycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an end-to-end optimization plan for [agent]. Include baseline analysis, prompt changes, adversarial tests, staged rollout, monitoring, rollback triggers, and a 30-day review.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate an advanced improvement program across testing and production.

output_examples.input: Review a support agent with low completion rates and frequent clarification requests.
output: Baseline: Measure completion rate, clarification frequency, factual errors, and response latency.
Priority failures: Ambiguous intent handling, incomplete answers, and weak escalation rules.
Next step: Add intent checks and escalation examples, then run a regression comparison.

output_examples.input: Plan an A/B test for a revised research agent prompt.
output: Compare the current and revised prompts on the same representative task set.
Score factual accuracy, citation quality, completion rate, latency, and token use.
Promote the revision only when quality improves without exceeding cost or safety limits.

output_examples.input: Define rollback criteria for an agent deployment.
output_examples.output: Rollback when task success drops materially, critical errors rise, safety violations appear, or cost exceeds the approved threshold.

best_practices: Change one major behavior at a time so evaluation results remain attributable.
Use representative failures, edge cases, and adversarial inputs in every regression suite.
Define acceptance and rollback thresholds before exposing users to a revised agent.
anti_patterns: Do not deploy prompt changes based only on a few favorable examples.
Do not compare variants with different tasks, rubrics, or evaluator instructions.
Do not collect user interaction data without authorization, redaction, and retention controls.

faq.question: Can this skill create a new agent?
faq.answer: No. It is designed to improve an existing agent with available metrics, feedback, or test cases.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It defines evaluation workflows and criteria, but execution depends on tools available in your environment.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the current prompt, representative tasks, failures, quality metrics, tool constraints, and deployment requirements.

faq.question: How many test cases are required?
faq.answer: Use enough representative cases for reliable comparison. Adjust sample size according to expected effects, risk, and available traffic.

faq.question: Can it improve safety performance?
faq.answer: It can define safety checks, adversarial tests, and rollout gates. Domain experts should approve high-risk safety criteria.

faq.question: How should private interaction data be handled?
faq.answer: Use authorized, minimized, redacted data with access controls and retention limits. Follow applicable privacy and security requirements.
